Hypothesis: We hypothesize that in HCC, oxidative stress accelerates tumor progression through two interdependent regulatory axes. The first axis is an established mechanism whereby oxidative stress elevates HBXIP levels, which in turn upregulates METTL3, leading to increased m6A modifications on key metabolic transcripts and on HIF-1α mRNA – resulting in enhanced metabolic reprogramming and tumor proliferation. The second, novel axis proposes that oxidative stress directly activates the METTL3/METTL14 complex via redox-sensitive modifications (potentially identified by mass spectrometry) that alter its substrate specificity. This activation enables selective m6A modification of a defined set of hypoxia-responsive long non-coding RNAs, exemplified by lncRNA-X. The m6A-marked lncRNA-X then binds more avidly to the m6A reader IGF2BP2, thereby stabilizing HIF1α mRNA. The resultant increase in HIF-1α protein levels promotes angiogenesis and establishes a self-reinforcing loop that further elevates oxidative stress. This integrated model will be tested using advanced techniques including m6A-seq, CLIP-seq, CRISPR-based epitranscriptomic interventions, and redox-proteomic assays to elucidate the molecular underpinnings of oxidative stress-mediated HCC progression.
Abstract: This study proposes a refined dual-axis model for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression under oxidative stress. In the first, well-established axis, oxidative stress upregulates HBXIP leading to enhanced METTL3 expression, which increases m6A modifications on metabolic transcripts, including HIF-1α mRNA, thereby promoting metabolic reprogramming and tumor growth. In the second, novel axis, oxidative stress is posited to directly induce redox-sensitive modifications in the METTL3/METTL14 complex, thereby fine-tuning its substrate specificity to selectively modify a subset of hypoxia-responsive long non-coding RNAs (e.g., lncRNA-X). This modification enhances the binding affinity of these lncRNAs for the m6A reader protein IGF2BP2, stabilizing HIF-1α mRNA. The accumulated HIF-1α protein fuels angiogenesis and further increases oxidative stress, creating a self-amplifying feedback loop. Importantly, this hypothesis leverages contemporary technologies such as m6A-seq, CLIP-seq, targeted CRISPR-mediated epitranscriptomic modulation, and mass spectrometry analyses to delineate redox modifications on METTL3/METTL14, thereby providing mechanistic insight into this dual regulatory system.
CausalChain: Oxidative stress -> Upregulation of HBXIP -> Increased METTL3 expression -> Enhanced m6A modifications on metabolic transcripts and HIF-1α mRNA -> Metabolic reprogramming and tumor growth || Oxidative stress -> Redox-sensitive modifications in METTL3/METTL14 -> Selective m6A tagging of hypoxia-responsive lncRNAs (e.g., lncRNA-X) -> Enhanced binding to IGF2BP2 -> Stabilization of HIF-1α mRNA -> Elevated HIF-1α protein -> Angiogenesis -> Further oxidative stress
